notes: The rule's obligation is that a condition the implementor specifies yields a 9x value. WiseOwl's relative condition (a character with no byte image) yields 91, documented at DOC-A.1-110, and the record is not written. The refuter's key-0 case is not this rule's: RelativeConnector.Write tests 'slot is < 1 or > HighestRelativeRecordNumber' on ONE line (line 342) and returns 34 for both. So the implementor's boundary is 1..highest (DOC-A.1-107), and key 0 is a write beyond the externally defined boundaries, status 24's case. That status-34 defect is kb/Work PB5125 (1985-GR-VIII.1.3.4-L2.3), and its fix (24 through the invalid-key path, no edition arm today) covers key 0 at the same line. The probe also shows the 34 persisting as a permanent error. ATTACK SURFACE: if a reader holds that record number 0 is not 'beyond' a boundary, key 0 becomes an implementor-defined condition and must answer 9x, which would make this row PARTIAL; the shared code line is the evidence that the implementor classes it as a boundary.

next.reason: 1985: "unsuccessfully executed as the result of a condition that is specified by the implementor."; 2023: "An implementor-defined condition exists. This condition shall not duplicate any other condition specified by another I-O status value.". Both define status 9x as implementor-defined. 2023 newly forbids it to duplicate another status condition. The 1985 rule letting the implementor choose among several values is not found in the candidates.
